title: Harlem house rent parties
summary: Rent parties paid about $10 a stop, grew from church suppers, and had dances like the Bump and the Grind.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: In regard to house rent parties in Harlem, on one of the tapes he said, well, they were just what they said they were. And here's some information from him that elucidates it further. He said they got about $10.00 a shot, would make stops at three or four different rent parties on a Saturday night. And they'd make the piano sound like an orchestra, the people would dance to the music. The dances had names like the Bump, the Grind, the Monkey Hunch. A lot of the dances young people are doing today aren't much different, according to J. C.

He said the rent parties really began from old-fashioned church suppers. Members of a congregation would get together in a good-sized railroad flat, have a feast prepared by ladies of the church. There'd be fried chicken, baked ham, pigs feet, gumbo and potato salad. Have I made anybody hungry? It only cost a nominal sum and the money was used to send the pastor on vacation or fix something in the church.
Well, as he said, rents skyrocketed and the idea came to borrow church suppers and raise money to pay the rent.
